title: Killed job is restarted by its scheduler

brief.headline: Database Guardian could not produce a grounded proposal
brief.what_broke: 12 session(s) waiting on locks. Root blocker(s): pid 150932 (batch_worker/batch_replayable_price_sync, idle in transaction, txn open 7.6s) blocks 1 session(s); last statement: SELECT 1
brief.who_is_affected: Checkout success 27% over 30s (88/120 failed) vs SLO 95%. Revenue run-rate $18,400/min; about $13,493/min at risk. Verification window 10s. The business tolerates at most 60s of degraded checkout.

options.description: Terminate the root blocker session (batch_worker/batch_replayable_price_sync, pid 150932) to release its locks.
Take no action; let the blocker finish and monitor checkout recovery.
options.cost: about $13,493/min of checkout revenue at risk while waiting

brief.recommendation: Checkout is at 27% success (BIZ-3) vs 95% SLO, losing ~$13,493/min (BIZ-3). The blocker batch_replayable_price_sync is BATCH_REPLAYABLE, may_interrupt, replay cost 2 min (BIZ-2). Trade-off (BIZ-4): waiting ~592s costs ~$133,224 and EXCEEDS the 60s tolerated degradation; terminating costs a 2-min replay. Waiting is not acceptable per I7. Termination is the business-preferred action for this replayable workload, pending change-calendar evidence (I2).

audit.report: The checkout flow degraded after a batch job (batch_replayable_price_sync) entered an idle transaction, blocking 12 sessions and causing success to drop to 27% (88/120 failed). The Database Guardian recommended waiting for the blocker to complete naturally, but the Continuity Guardian rejected this because the expected remaining runtime (~592s) exceeds the 60-second business tolerance for degraded checkout, costing an estimated $133k in lost revenue. Escalation to the pricing team was required because the Database Guardian could not ground its proposal in the independent authority's invariants.
audit.root_cause: A replayable batch job (batch_replayable_price_sync) became the root blocker, holding an idle transaction that stalled checkout sessions and violated the 60-second degradation tolerance.
lessons: Terminate idle batch_replayable_price_sync early: The job is marked may_interrupt and idempotent; killing it after ~8s of idle-in-transaction avoids the $133k revenue loss while only incurring a 2-minute replay cost.
audit.negotiation_critique: The Database Guardian prioritized natural completion, citing the 60s business tolerance, but underestimated the blocker's remaining runtime and overestimated the likelihood of finish within the window. The Continuity Guardian correctly identified the revenue-risk trade-off but had to object on the exceeded tolerance, triggering escalation rather than proposing an early-terminate alternative.
follow_ups: Add a dashboard alert when a BATCH_REPLAYABLE job exceeds 5s idle-in-transaction during checkout hours.
Run a one-time replay of batch_replayable_price_sync to confirm idempotency and validate the 2-minute recovery cost.
Update the lock-graph probe to surface idle-in-transaction duration as a primary field for batch jobs.

proposal.risk_assessment: The blocker may not finish soon, prolonging checkout timeouts. Revenue at risk accumulates during the wait. However, terminating the batch job risks interrupting a replayable price sync, which could cause downstream pricing inconsistencies.
